questions: Q1: Should PLAY replace EXECUTE in VALID_MODES or should both be accepted?
Q2: Does the CLI need new Play-specific subcommands for MVP?

answers.answer: Replace EXECUTE with PLAY. The server will reject EXECUTE after the API validation update. Zero EXECUTE tickets exist — no backward-compatibility concern for scripts. Keeping both values would allow users to specify a mode the server rejects, creating a confusing failure experience.
evidence: Production DB: 0 EXECUTE tickets across 846 total
Server ticketModeEnum will exclude EXECUTE after update

answers.answer: No. The CLI's ticket creation with --mode PLAY is sufficient for MVP. Play-specific subcommands (preview, execute, rollback) are deferred to the governance/execution follow-up ticket. The ticket description says 'Use normal Helix ticket system to create a Play'.
evidence: Ticket description item 1: 'Use normal Helix ticket system to create a Play'
MVP scope is mode scaffolding, not execution engine
continue.ts --dry-run is mode-agnostic client-side preview — no PLAY changes needed

statement: The CLI needs a single-file change: replace EXECUTE with PLAY in the VALID_MODES tuple and update the help text in create.ts. No new subcommands or flags for MVP. The CLI is a thin client — server enforces platform restrictions. This is the smallest change surface of all repos.
